'''Michael Liam McQuillan''' is a Scottish [[mathematician]] studying [[algebraic geometry]].  As of 2019 he is professor at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]].

==Career==
Michael McQuillan received the doctorate in 1992 at  [[Harvard University]] under [[Barry Mazur]] ("Division points on semi-Abelian varieties").<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.math.harvard.edu/graduate/dissertations/ |publisher=Harvard University |title=Harvard Department of Mathematics PhD Dissertations Archival Listing}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=18812}}</ref>

In 1995, McQuillan proved the [[Mordell–Lang conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=McQuillan |first=Michael |date=1995-12-01 |title=Division points on semi-abelian varieties |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01241125 |journal=Inventiones mathematicae |language=en |volume=120 |issue=1 |pages=143–159 |doi=10.1007/BF01241125 |issn=1432-1297|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1996, MacQuillan gave a new proof of a conjecture of [[André Bloch (mathematician)|André Bloch]] (1926) about holomorphic curves in closed subvarieties of Abelian varieties,<ref>{{cite journal | last=McQuillan | first=Michael Liam | title=A new proof of the Bloch conjecture | journal=[[Journal of Algebraic Geometry]] | volume=5 | year=1996 | pages=107–117 | mr=1358036 | issue=1}} Bloch's proof was incomplete.  Ochiai proved special cases. The first proof was by Mark Green, who presented a further proof with  Phillip Griffiths in 1979.</ref> proved a conjecture of  [[Shoshichi Kobayashi]] (about the  Kobayashi-hyperbolicity of generic hypersurfaces of high degree in projective ''n''-dimensional space) in the three-dimensional case<ref>{{cite journal | last=McQuillan | first=Michael Liam | title=Holomorphic curves on hyperplane sections of 3-folds | journal=[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]] |volume=9 | year=1999 | pages=370–392 | issue=2 | mr=1692470 | doi=10.1007/s000390050091}} At about the same time [[Jean-Pierre Demailly]] and J. El-Goul also achieved similar results.</ref> and achieved partial results on a conjecture of [[Mark Lee Green|Mark Green]] and [[Phillip Griffiths]] (which states that a holomorphic curve on an algebraic surface of general type with  <math>c_{1}^2 > c_2</math> cannot be Zariski-dense).<ref>{{cite journal | last=McQuillan | first=Michael Liam | title=Diophantine approximations and foliations | journal= [[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]] | volume=87 | year=1998 | pages=121–174 | mr=1659270 | url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=PMIHES_1998__87__121_0| doi=10.1007/BF02698862 }}</ref>

From 1996 to 2001 he was a post-doctoral Research Fellow at [[All Souls College]] of the [[University of Oxford]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asc.ox.ac.uk/person/220|title=Dr Michael McQuillan|publisher=All Souls College}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asc.ox.ac.uk/research/8|title=All Souls College: Mathematics|publisher=All Souls College}}</ref> and in 2009 was Professor at the [[University of Glasgow]] as well as Advanced Research Fellow of the British  [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]]. As of 2019 he is professor at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]] and an editor of the ''European Journal of Mathematics''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/40879/editors|title=European Journal of Mathematics: Editors|publisher=Springer}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2000 McQuillan received the [[European Mathematical Society#2000 prizes|EMS Prize]], which was announced from the European Congress of Mathematics in July 2000, for his work:{{blockquote|Michael McQuillan has created the method of dynamic diophantine approximation, which has led to a series of remarkable results in complex geometry of algebraic varieties. Among these results one can mention a new proof of Bloch’s conjecture on holomorphic curves in closed subvarieties of abelian varieties, the proof of the conjecture of Green and Griffiths that a holomorphic curve in a surface of general type cannot be Zariski-dense, and the hyperbolicity of generic hypersurfaces of high degree in projective 3-space (the Kobayashi conjecture).<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200009/people.pdf
|date=2000
|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]
|title=Mathematics People (excerpt from ''Notices'')
}}</ref>}}

In 2001 he was awarded the  [[Whitehead Prize]] of the  [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations01/mcquillan.html
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040822202940/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations01/mcquillan.html
|archive-date=2004-08-22
|title=Citation for Michael McQuillan (Laudatio for the Whitehead Prize)
|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]
|date=2001-07-02
}}</ref> In 2002 he was invited speaker at the  [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Beijing]] (''Integrating <math>\partial \bar{\partial}</math>'').<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|publisher=International Mathematical Union|access-date=2024-06-12}}</ref> In 2001 he received the  [[Sir Edmund Whittaker Memorial Prize|Whittaker Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/EMS/EMSWhittakerPrize/|title=EMS Whittaker Prize|work=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive|publisher=University of St Andrews|access-date=2024-06-12}}</ref>
